policies.summary: If a local ordinance would preclude or inhibit a facility that has received a Commission certificate of public convenience and necessity, the facility may proceed anyway.

No city, village, town or county may restrict a solar or wind energy system unless the restriction protects public health or safety, does not significantly raise cost or cut efficiency, or allows a comparable alternative; local wind rules may not be stricter than the Commission's wind siting rules.

A wind or solar plant of 100 MW or more (a large electric generating facility) needs a certificate of public convenience and necessity from the Public Service Commission; smaller plants not built by a public utility are permitted by cities, villages, towns and counties within state limits on local restrictions.

Commission rules set the wind siting standards that local ordinances may not exceed and that the Commission applies to its own reviews: turbine setbacks of the lesser of 1,250 feet or 3.1 times blade tip height from non-participating residences and occupied community buildings, 1.1 times tip height from non-participating property lines and roads, and noise limits of 50 dBA by day and 45 dBA at night.

restrictions.description: Pause on development of data centers and battery energy storage systems in unincorporated Door County to allow investigation, planning, and regulation of potential impacts; Board may extend by separate action. Active as of 2026-09-23. Confirmed via Door County's own official board minutes (reproduced in the June 23, 2026 agenda packet): Resolution 2026-41 was adopted by voice vote at the May 26, 2026 County Board meeting, imposing a moratorium on data centers and battery energy storage systems in unincorporated Door County "for a period of up to twelve (12) months from the date of this resolution," i.e. through approximately 2027-05-26, with the Board retaining the right to extend by separate action. No extension, repeal, or rescission was found as of 2026-09-23. Legal basis: Resolution 2026-41 (Door County Board of Supervisors).

Stops receipt of applications and issuance of zoning-related permits for medium and large data centers and battery storage facilities. Active as of 2026-07-31; a motion to return the measure to committee failed 3-10 before adoption. Legal basis: Resolution 07-26-04 (Monroe County Board).

County currently lacks local zoning regulations for data centers, battery energy storage systems, or large-scale solar; officials cite fire hazards (BESS), noise/vibration from cooling units, light pollution, water/air quality, stormwater runoff, and traffic impacts. Pending as of 2026-09-23. The Vilas County Zoning & Planning Committee held a public hearing on the proposed ordinance on 2026-09-23 (the date of this research); the full County Board of Supervisors is scheduled to vote at its October 27, 2026 meeting. As drafted, the moratorium would freeze acceptance, review, or approval of development permits for data centers, BESS, and solar energy systems exceeding one acre, for 12 months, with exemptions for solar installations of one acre or less, ordinary maintenance/repairs, emergency utility restoration, and projects already holding valid county permits. Legal basis: Proposed Vilas County ordinance (draft; number not yet assigned per reviewed sources), Zoning & Planning Committee public hearing held 2026-09-23 under Wis. Stat. §§ 59.02(2), 59.03(2)(a), and 59.69.
